checked.note: Microsoft's .NET releases index gives .NET 8.0 "eol-date" 2026-11-10 (endoflife.date agrees), so 10 days from the finding; 'planned' with no fix version fits an approaching end of support.

MSRC: Chromium CVE (Skia memory corruption) fixed in Microsoft Edge 156.0.4314.56; Edge security release notes show Stable 156.0.4314.56 on 2026-10-29 with Chromium security fixes, so .50 is affected.
MSRC: Chromium CVE (use after free in FileSystem) fixed in Microsoft Edge 156.0.4314.56, the Stable release of 2026-10-29; installed .50 predates it. Stable .58 followed on 2026-10-30.
MSRC lists SQL Server 2022 GDR fixed by KB5128493 at 16.0.1210.3; the KB page names CVE-2026-83945 and that build. Installed 16.0.1000.6 is RTM, which is on the GDR path.

MSRC says the check stays opt-in on all supported Windows 10/11 and "the reg key must be set" in both Wintrust\Config and Wow6432Node; both unset here. 26H2 isn't in the MSRC table but the text covers it. Aside: MSRC corrected the type to REG_DWORD; the agent's remediation writes REG_SZ.

'2' is the count of adapters whose NetbiosOptions isn't 2; Microsoft's doc says only 2 disables NetBIOS (0 uses DHCP, 1 enables). Caveat: an adapter at 0 is off only if DHCP says so, which the check can't see.
